$comment: TF-C78 (D-CSUBSET-NOINLINE): GNU `__attribute__((noinline))` is HONORED — the source directive reaches a real sink (`attributeSemantics.effects` verb `noInline` -> SymbolRecord.isNoInline -> HirNoInlineMap -> MirFunc.noInline -> the inliner's §2.9 legality gate, rule 2b) — and the honoring COMPOSES with the SHIPPED release optimizer across all four targets. All four spellings appear in one program: mode-2 (after the type), mode-3 (specifier prefix), the dunder form `__noinline__`, and PROTOTYPE-ONLY (definition bare, reaching MIR solely through the post-Pass-1.5 proto/def OR-merge). add_five(0)=5 -> times_two=10 -> minus_three=7 -> declared_first=8; 8*5+2 = 42. ★★ WHAT THIS EXAMPLE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM. Inlining is SEMANTICS-PRESERVING, so NO exit code can distinguish inlined from not-inlined, and every runtime probe that appears to (function-address comparison, stack-depth measurement) either invokes undefined behavior or TAKES THE CALLEE'S ADDRESS — which makes the inliner refuse under §2.9 rule 4 instead, rendering the check vacuous. Rather than ship a check that cannot fail, this example witnesses the COMPOSITION (four spellings parse, reach the sink, and the refusal still yields a correct runnable program under the real shipped pipeline on every target; a refusal that broke codegen, mis-threaded an argument or desynchronized the call graph lands here as a wrong exit code), and the APPLIED FACT is asserted where it is observable — at MIR tier by `MirLoweringCSubsetLinkage.NoInlineSurvivesShippedReleasePipeline` (which loads release.pipeline.json BY NAME and asserts the Call instruction SURVIVES), `Inlining.NoInlineCalleeIsNotInlined` + its flag-clear twin, and `MirRebuildHelper.RebuildFunctionPreservesNoInline`. That split is the honest one: an example arm claiming to prove non-inlining by exit code would be exactly the vacuous check the gnu_aligned_attribute example was corrected for. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE, MEASURED end-to-end on a real arm64 binary, TWO ways: (a) delete `inlining.cpp` rule 2b; (b) keep rule 2b and drop ONLY the `src_.funcNoInline(oldFn)` argument in `mir_rebuild_helper.cpp`. Both produce the SAME broken output — helpers spliced away, `main` folded to a single `mov x29, #0x2a` — because Inlining runs first in each of the release pipeline's 4 iterations and any rebuild between them clears an unpropagated flag. The two are INDISTINGUISHABLE in the emitted code, which is why the propagation carries its own dedicated pin rather than relying on the refusal pin. ★ The `release` arm is MANDATORY, not decoration: this is an optimizer×feature composition, and a baseline-only example would leave the one interaction that matters unwitnessed. ★ The whole file is VERIFIED clang-clean (`-fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -isysroot $(xcrun --show-sdk-path)`, zero errors, zero warnings) and the clang -O2 binary independently exits 42, so the expected exit code is ground truth from a real toolchain rather than merely what DSS happens to produce.
